title: 2026-10-28_KrustyLoader_Incident_Response_Scenario_55e
description: Investigate a KrustyLoader malware compromise on a victim host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: KrustyLoader is a Rust-based malware linked to Ivanti ConnectSecure compromises. It is designed to download and execute a Sliver backdoor. The malware exploits vulnerabilities CVE-2024-21887 and CVE-2023-46805 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You are an incident responder with access to the victim host `victim` (IP: 192.168.120.10) using the credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

To start the scenario, ENTER the passkey 'start'.
levels.local_content:
You are an incident responder with access to the victim host `victim` (IP: 192.168.120.10) using the credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

To start the scenario, ENTER the passkey 'start'.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Scheduled Task
levels.content: While reviewing the victim host, you notice unusual system behavior. Investigate the scheduled tasks or timers to identify any suspicious or unauthorized execution mechanisms.
levels.solution: Check systemd timers and services for any unusual entries. Look for the `session-mgr.timer` and `session-mgr.service` files in `/etc/systemd/system/`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check systemd timers and services for any unusual entries.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers and services that might have been recently added or modified.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Focus on the `/etc/systemd/system/` directory for any suspicious files.

levels.title: Analyze Suspicious Dropped Files
levels.content: Examine the victim host for any files that appear to have been introduced by malicious software. Focus on directories that may have been created to conceal malicious files or payloads.
levels.solution: Look for recently created directories and files, especially those in unusual locations. Check the `/tmp/.session` directory for suspicious files.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for recently created directories and files, especially those in unusual locations.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Pay attention to directories like `/tmp/` which are commonly used to store temporary files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check for hidden directories or files within `/tmp/`.

levels.title: Identify Remote Access Component
levels.content: Determine if there is a component responsible for establishing unauthorized remote access on the victim host. Analyze any scripts or executables that might be used for this purpose.
levels.solution: Investigate scripts in suspicious directories and check their contents for remote access functionality. The `rat.sh` script in `/tmp/.session` is responsible for establishing remote access.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate scripts in suspicious directories and check their contents for remote access functionality.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for scripts that might be establishing network connections or listening on specific ports.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the contents of the `rat.sh` script in `/tmp/.session/` for any suspicious network activity.
